root_cause.text: The mm/slub krealloc/kvrealloc fallback logic copied the old allocation size without first reliably initializing `ks`/`orig_size` and without capping the copy to `new_size`, so forced reallocations for NUMA/alignment could copy 0 bytes or overflow the new smaller buffer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves old-size calculation above the `__GFP_THISNODE`/NUMA `goto alloc_new` in `__do_krealloc()`, and changes `memcpy(ret, ..., orig_size ?: ks)` to `memcpy(ret, ..., min(new_size, (size_t)(orig_size ?: ks)))` plus `memcpy(n, ..., ksize(p))` to `memcpy(n, ..., min(size, ksize(p)))`; the commit message explicitly states the early jump left `ks` and `orig_size` uninitialized and that shrinking with forced alignment used the old size, causing out-of-bounds writes.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop krealloc from unnecessarily reallocating existing memory when __GFP_THISNODE requests a different NUMA node.
intent_record.what: A conditional block and its explanatory comment were removed from __do_krealloc(); specifically, the code that checked for __GFP_THISNODE with a valid nid different from the current allocation's page node and then jumped to alloc_new was deleted.
intent_record.how: krealloc will no longer force a new allocation solely because __GFP_THISNODE requests a different NUMA node than the one backing the existing pointer, so existing allocations can now be preserved in that case instead of being reallocated onto the requested node.

intent_record.intent_summary: Force krealloc to reallocate onto the requested NUMA node when __GFP_THISNODE is set, even if the existing buffer is already large enough.
intent_record.what: A new conditional block and explanatory comment were added before the existing size check in __do_krealloc(). The code now tests whether __GFP_THISNODE is set, nid is valid (not NUMA_NO_NODE), and the current allocation's NUMA node differs from nid using page_to_nid(virt_to_page(p)); if all are true, execution jumps to alloc_new.
intent_record.how: This changes krealloc behavior so that even when the existing allocation is already large enough, a new allocation is forced if the caller requested allocation on a specific NUMA node with __GFP_THISNODE and the current object resides on a different node. It prevents silently keeping memory on the wrong NUMA node under a strict node-local allocation request.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix __do_krealloc() to copy only up to the new allocation size, avoiding overflow when reallocating to a smaller buffer.
intent_record.what: The third argument to memcpy() in __do_krealloc() was changed from copying orig_size ?: ks bytes unconditionally to copying min(new_size, (size_t)(orig_size ?: ks)) bytes.
intent_record.how: This limits the copy during krealloc to the smaller of the requested new allocation size and the original source size, preventing writes past the end of the new buffer when shrinking an allocation while still preserving existing data up to the new size.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix kvrealloc copy size to avoid overflowing the new allocation when reallocating to a smaller buffer.
intent_record.what: The third argument to memcpy() in kvrealloc_node_align_noprof() was changed from ksize(p) to min(size, ksize(p)) when copying data from the old allocation p to the new allocation n.
intent_record.how: This limits the copy length to the smaller of the requested new size and the old allocation size, preventing reads and writes beyond the new buffer size when reallocating to a smaller size while still preserving existing data up to the new allocation limit.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix reallocation helpers to limit copied bytes to the new allocation size when shrinking buffers, preventing overflow into the new allocation.

relevance_review.reason: The change avoids unnecessary krealloc reallocations for __GFP_THISNODE/NUMA-node mismatches, but it does not address the root cause in the fallback copy logic: uninitialized ks/orig_size or failing to cap the copied size to new_size.

The group introduces the forced krealloc reallocation path for NUMA (__GFP_THISNODE) requests, which is exactly the scenario that triggers the fallback logic implicated in the bug. Since the vulnerability occurs during forced reallocations, this change is directly tied to the root cause.

The group directly addresses a key root cause element: the fallback reallocation logic copied the old allocation size without capping it to new_size. Limiting copied bytes in __do_krealloc() and kvrealloc when shrinking prevents overflow into the smaller new buffer.

candidates.rationale: This copy uses orig_size or ks without ensuring they were reliably initialized for all fallback paths, and it does not cap the length to new_size. That directly enables copying 0 bytes when size state is wrong or overflowing a newly smaller allocation during forced reallocation.
This copies the full old allocation size into the new buffer without limiting the copy to the requested new size, so shrinking reallocations can overflow the destination.

This condition only forced allocation of a new object when the requested size exceeded ks. As a result, NUMA/alignment-forced reallocations could take fallback paths where later copy logic relied on ks/orig_size not being properly prepared for the reallocation case.

vuln_statements.explanation: This fallback copy in __do_krealloc() is the direct vulnerable operation: it uses orig_size or ks even when size state was not reliably initialized for forced reallocation paths, and it does not cap the copy length to new_size, enabling either zero-byte copy or overflow into a smaller newly allocated buffer.

This kvrealloc fallback copies the full old allocation size into the new allocation without limiting the length to the requested new size, so shrinking reallocations can overflow the destination buffer.

This condition failed to force reallocation for NUMA/alignment cases unless the new size exceeded ks, allowing execution to reach fallback copy paths where ks/orig_size were not properly prepared for the forced reallocation scenario described in the root cause.

The vulnerable root cause was: old size used in fallback copy without reliable initialization of `ks`/`orig_size`, and copy not capped to `new_size`. In this commit, the problematic uninitialized state is addressed: `size_t ks = 0;` and `int orig_size = 0;` explicitly initialize both variables. Thus the copy is effectively bounded by the old size and cannot overflow the new buffer in this shown logic. Therefore the vulnerable construct is absent here, and this version already contains the fix.
